name: Musick Point / Te Naupata
access: End of Musick Point Rd, Bucklands Beach. Small car park at the esplanade, 2 min walk to the clifftop.
best: 50-60 m cliffs, WWII radio-station buildings, harbour + Rangitoto/Waiheke backdrop. Best cinematic and long-range site east of the city.
hazards: Cliff edge, onshore sea breeze, salt spray, golfers on Pakuranga GC (keep clear), no recovery if you ditch in the harbour.
note: Reserve + point are public; the golf course is a lease, so launch from the esplanade/point grass, not the fairways. Log the flight on AirShare.
launch: Car park at the end of Musick Point Rd; 2 min walk to the grass above the harbour.

name: Waitawa Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Waitawa Bay Rd off Kawakawa-Orere Rd, ~50 min from CBD. Road-end car parks, MTB trailhead.
best: Coastal farmland, regenerating bush, coves and ridges - the most wild flying inside an hour of the city.
hazards: Exposed ridgelines = strong wind, stock, MTB riders, patchy phone coverage in gullies.
note: Not on the council's banned list, so a regional-park drone permit is obtainable - apply through council 'Make an enquiry online' before you go.
launch: Road-end car parks on Waitawa Bay Rd; fly from the MTB trailhead clearing.

name: Kawakawa Bay
access: Kawakawa Bay Rd to the boat ramp and beach reserve, ~50 min from CBD.
best: Beach, rocky headlands, bush edge and moored boats - coastal freestyle and cinematic.
hazards: Boat ramp traffic in summer, shorebirds on the sand, tidal currents, salt.
note: Quietest easy-access east coast beach. Weekday mornings you will often have it to yourself. Pin is the beach and boat ramp area; the old pin was 500 m out in the bay.
launch: Boat ramp car park at the end of Kawakawa Bay Rd; fly from the beach reserve beside it.

name: Te Puru Park / Maraetai
access: Te Puru Park car park off Maraetai Dr, ~40 min from CBD.
best: Water, wharf and pohutukawa coastline with Waiheke and Ponui across the strait.
hazards: Beachgoers and kids in summer, ferry/boat traffic, shorebirds.
note: No permit needed (local park). Best at dawn - the beach gets busy from about 10am in summer.
launch: Te Puru Park car park off Maraetai Dr; fly from the field above the beach.

name: Stonefields Quarry / Heritage Trail
land: Auckland Council local park / heritage trail
access: Stonefields Ave or College Rd, 15 min from CBD. Street parking, short walk to the old quarry face.
best: Urban freestyle: sheer quarry rock walls, wetland boardwalk, terraced levels, Sky Tower and Maungarei sightlines.
hazards: Dog walkers and runners, houses overlooking the quarry, and the 20 m building / 30 m people rules bite here.
note: The best close-to-town freestyle site. Fly the quarry bowl and boardwalk early morning and log the flight on AirShare as council land. The old pin was the Stonefields suburb centroid. Pin is the quarry wetland at Maungarei Springs; the old pin sat in the middle of the housing development.
launch: Street parking on Stonefields Ave or College Rd; fly from the path edge at the old quarry floor.

name: Panmure Basin
access: Basin View or Ireland Rd car parks, 20 min from CBD. Flat 1.6 km boardwalk loop.
best: Volcanic crater lagoon - smooth over-water lines, boardwalk, Maungarei as a backdrop.
hazards: Constant walkers and runners, water (no retrieval), swans and ducks, tide.
note: Great for smooth cinematic passes at low tide. Keep 30 m from boardwalk users and stay away from the playground. Pin is Panmure Basin Domain on the shore; the old pin was the middle of the lagoon.
launch: Car park at the Basin View / Ireland Rd end; fly from the reserve grass on the northern shore of the lagoon.

name: Point England Reserve
access: Point England Rd, 20 min from CBD. Large grass car park.
best: Big open launch with estuary, Rangitoto and Tamaki River lines - good for maiden flights and long-range runs.
hazards: Sports fields in use (no flying over), dogs off lead, shorebirds at the estuary edge.
note: The most forgiving space in central-east: huge line of sight, flat, clean airspace, and you can stand well clear of people. The old pin was on Rowena Crescent, on the inland edge of the reserve. Pin is the reserve as Google Maps plots it, on the estuary side.
launch: Grass car park off Point England Rd; fly from the open field facing the harbour.

name: Waiatarua Reserve
land: Auckland Council local reserve (official dog park)
access: Abbotts Way / Grand Dr, 15 min from CBD. Car park off Grand Dr.
best: Wetland and boardwalk with open lawn - good for low, slow cinematic and proximity practice.
hazards: It is an official dog park - dogs will chase a low quad. Wetland means no retrieval.
note: Legal with clean airspace, but dog traffic makes it a dawn-only spot for anything low.
launch: Car park off Grand Dr; set up on the mown grass beside the wetland.

name: Glendowie Park / Churchill Park
access: Glendowie Rd or Riddell Rd, 20 min from CBD.
best: Clifftop park with harbour views; Churchill Park's karaka grove 400 m north gives tree lines and shade.
hazards: Ridge wind, dog walkers, sports fields on weekends.
note: Solid quick local session when you do not want to drive east.
launch: Park on Glendowie Rd or Riddell Rd; fly from the clifftop grass.

name: Monte Cecilia Park
access: Hillsborough Rd, 20 min from CBD. Car park at Pah Homestead.
best: Huge mature trees, rolling lawns, Pah Homestead facade and Manukau Harbour views - cinematic rather than freestyle.
hazards: Weddings and events at the homestead, dog walkers, big trees eat 5.8 GHz if you go behind them.
note: Best central spot for pretty footage rather than bando flying. Check the homestead is not mid-event.
launch: Park at the Pah Homestead car park on Hillsborough Rd; fly from the open parkland south of the house.

name: Coyle Park / Meola Reef
access: Point Chevalier Rd, 20 min from CBD. Car park at the park.
best: Clifftop over the Waitemata, Meola Reef at low tide and the full city skyline - the best skyline shot in this list.
hazards: Strong onshore wind, mudflats at low tide, dog walkers.
note: Sunset skyline runs from the clifftop are the reason to come. Wind is the limiting factor.
launch: Car park inside Coyle Park off Point Chevalier Rd, then a 2 min walk to the grass above the cliff.

name: Mangemangeroa Reserve
access: Somerville Rd, Shelly Park, 30 min from CBD. Walk the valley track to the estuary.
best: Bush valley and mangrove estuary - tight technical lines and a completely different look to the beaches.
hazards: Dense canopy means LOS and video dropout, mud, no retrieval in the mangroves.
note: Genuinely quiet. Bring a spotter - the bush swallows quads and sightlines. The old pin sat on a residential street in Cockle Bay, 2.9 km north of the reserve. Pin is the reserve as Google Maps plots it; the main walkway entrance is at the Sandspit Road end about 1.5 km north.
launch: Somerville Rd entrance; walk the valley track about 10 min to the estuary boardwalk.

name: Eastern Beach
access: The Esplanade, Eastern Beach, 30 min from CBD.
best: Long pohutukawa-backed beach, rocks at the north end, Rangitoto across the water.
hazards: Swimmers in summer, shorebirds nesting Sep-Mar at the north end, salt.
note: Better than Bucklands for flying because you can walk away from the crowd at the northern rocks.
launch: Car park on The Esplanade; fly from the sand at the northern end.

name: Sunkist Bay / Beachlands
access: Sunkist Bay Rd, Beachlands, 40 min from CBD.
best: Small quiet bay, moored boats, pine and pohutukawa, flat water at high tide.
hazards: Boat moorings, shellfish beds at low tide, and nobody around if you need help retrieving a quad.
note: Low-key local spot - combine it with Maraetai/Te Puru in one trip. Pin is on the sand at the head of the bay.
launch: End of Sunkist Bay Rd, Beachlands; fly from the beach reserve.

name: Orakei Basin
access: Orakei Rd or Upland Rd, 10 min from CBD. Boardwalk loop.
best: Tidal crater lagoon ringed by bush, 10 minutes from town - water lines with the city behind.
hazards: Inside the Auckland Hospital 4 km ring: needs Part 101 certificate + observer + AirShare log.
note: Sits in the Southern Automatic Authorisation Zone - automatic approval ONLY with a Part 101 qualification from a Part 141 provider and an observer. Without the cert, do not. Pin is Orakei Basin Domain on the shore; the old pin was the middle of the lagoon.
launch: Enter from Orakei Rd or Upland Rd; fly from the grass beside the boardwalk.

name: Omana Beach
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Omana Dr, Maraetai, 45 min from CBD.
best: Pohutukawa-fringed beach, headland, farmland and Waiheke views - postcard FPV.
hazards: Farm animals, beachgoers, permit conditions.
note: Only worth it if you are already getting a regional-park permit for Waitawa - do both in one application.
launch: Car park on Omana Dr; fly from the beach reserve.

name: Lloyd Elsmore Park
access: Sir Lloyd Dr, Pakuranga, 25 min from CBD.
best: Huge flat park - good for tuning, GPS tests and race practice when the fields are empty.
hazards: Sports fields in use, netball and pool crowds, cricket nets.
note: Not scenic. Useful as a test-and-tune field, not a destination.
launch: Car park off Sir Lloyd Dr; fly from the edge of the sports fields.

name: Fearon Park
best: Big open grass for fixed-wing and tuning flights, with a carpark and toilets on site.
hazards: Dog walkers, boundary trees, and weekend sport on the field.
note: Mount Roskill. The submitted pin sat on Rodney farmland about 45 km north, so the coordinates are corrected to the actual park. Flat, open rugby field with a carpark by the tennis club; best on weekday mornings when it is empty.
access: Carpark off Fearon Ave by the tennis club; toilets on site.
avoid: Weekend sport, and the 07:00-09:00 dog-walker window
launch: Car park off Fearon Ave by the tennis courts; fly from the top field.

name: Cockle Bay Beach
access: Cockle Bay Beach, off Shelly Beach Parade, Howick.
best: Sheltered bay with a small beach, rocks and a jetty — calm water in most winds.
hazards: Swimmers and kayakers in summer, moored boats, shellfish beds at low tide.
note: Better in an easterly than the bigger Howick beaches.
launch: Car park off Shelly Beach Parade; fly from the beach reserve.

name: Shelly Park Beach
access: Shelly Park Beach, end of Sandspit Rd.
best: Mangrove estuary and sand flats — flat water, big skies, very few people.
hazards: Mud and mangroves at low tide, shorebirds Sep-Mar, no shade.
note: Pairs with Mangemangeroa next door; fly the estuary on a rising tide.
launch: End of Sandspit Rd; fly from the estuary beach.

name: Mellons Bay Beach
access: Mellons Bay Beach, off Bleakhouse Rd, Howick.
best: Pohutukawa-backed beach with cliffs at the southern end and Rangitoto on the horizon.
hazards: Cliff updraughts, swimmers in summer, narrow beach at high tide.
note: Quieter than Howick Beach and a better shoreline for low passes.
launch: Car park off Bleakhouse Rd; fly from the beach.

name: Howick Beach
access: Howick Beach, off Granger Rd; car park at the end.
best: Long sandy beach, jetty and the Howick village edge — easy access for a quick flight.
hazards: Busy in summer, jetty users, moored boats.
note: Convenience spot — the beach is the draw, the crowds are the cost.
launch: Car park at the end of Granger Rd; fly from the sand.

name: Macleans Park
access: Macleans Park, off Macleans Rd, Bucklands Beach.
best: Big sports fields with bush edges — good for tuning and short-range practice.
hazards: School and club sport, cricket nets, dog walkers.
note: A practical field rather than a scenic spot.
launch: Car park off Macleans Rd; fly from the top field.

name: Umupuia Beach
access: Umupuia Beach, off Maraetai Coast Rd; gravel car park at the end.
best: Wide tidal estuary, sand flats and farmland — empty most days, huge open lines.
hazards: Tidal flats cut you off, soft sand, stock nearby, patchy phone coverage.
note: One of the quietest beaches inside the Auckland boundary.
launch: Gravel car park at the end of Maraetai Coast Rd; fly from the beach.

name: Duder Regional Park
land: Auckland Council regional park - PERMIT required
access: Duder Regional Park, off North Rd, Maraetai; gate at the end of the road.
best: Coastal farmland, cliffs and empty beaches — the best scenery on the Pohutukawa Coast.
hazards: Stock, cliff edges, permit conditions, no water or shelter.
note: Needs an Auckland Council regional park permit — worth it for the cliff lines.
launch: Gate at the end of North Rd; walk 15 min to the beach, or fly from the open paddock by the car park.

name: Meola Reef Reserve
access: Meola Rd, Point Chevalier; park at the reserve entrance.
best: Reef and harbour-edge flying with the city skyline behind you; shallow water at low tide.
hazards: Dog walkers early and late, motorway noise, mudflats at low tide, harbour traffic.
note: A dog park on the point — fine for a quick session, not a destination.
launch: Reserve entrance car park on Meola Rd; fly from the grass above the reef.

name: Eric Armishaw Park
access: Eric Armishaw Park, off Great North Rd, Waterview.
best: Quiet harbour-side reserve with open grass and a long water line toward the bridge.
hazards: Shared-path cyclists, dog walkers, tidal mud.
note: Overshadowed by Point Chevalier but emptier and easier to park.
launch: Car park off Great North Rd, Waterview; fly from the reserve grass by the inlet.

name: Western Springs Park
access: Great North Rd or Motions Rd; park at the stadium end.
best: Big open lawns and a lake — good for tuning and low-altitude practice, not scenery.
hazards: Very busy paths, geese, sports events, motorway on the boundary.
note: A test-and-tune field. Don't expect solitude.
launch: Stadium-end car park off Motions Rd; fly from the grass beside the lake.

name: Keith Hay Park
access: Keith Hay Park, off Hillsborough Rd, Mount Roskill.
best: Large flat sports fields with room for gate practice and long sightlines.
hazards: Sports fields in use most evenings and weekends, netball crowds.
note: Useful when Fearon Park is busy — same area, more space.
launch: Car park off Hillsborough Rd; fly from the edge of the sports fields.
